annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and finite matrix formalization of the exact displayed identity used to derive Theorem 1(7)

assumptions: Rinv is a certified right inverse of R.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P11 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P11 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p11_t2_orthogonality_defect_identity {n : Nat} (A dA Q R Rinv : P11Matrix n) (hQR : p11MatMul n Q R = A + dA) (hInv : p11MatMul n R Rinv = p11Identity n) : p11OrthogonalityDefect Q = p11MatMul n (p11MatMul n (p11Transpose Rinv) (p11DefectCore A dA R)) Rinv
formal_statement.plain_language: The loss-of-orthogonality matrix is exactly the inverse-transpose conjugation of the normal-equation residual minus the three perturbation-product terms.

informal_proof: Use the right inverse to rewrite Q as (A+DeltaA)Rinv and the identity as Rinv-transpose times R-transpose R times Rinv. Expand the two transposes and collect the normal-equation and perturbation terms in the paper's displayed order.
informal_statement: The exact inverse-conjugated orthogonality-defect identity displayed in the proof of Theorem 1(7).

paper_source.local_path: paper_bencmark/reference_papers/P11_A note on the error analysis of classical Gram–Schmidt.pdf

paper_version: published journal version; volume 105, issue 2, 2006, printed pages 299-313

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen MatrixAlgebra object supplies multiplication, identity, associativity, and transpose adapters, but no declaration derives the paper's residual-to-orthogonality identity from QR=A+DeltaA and an inverse certificate.

tier_rationale: The L proof combines NumStability.matMul_assoc, NumStability.matMul_id_right, NumStability.matTranspose_matMul, and NumStability.matTranspose_id from NumStability/Analysis/MatrixAlgebra.lean with the paper-specific substitution QR=A+DeltaA and noncommutative expansion.
